title: Pharaoh Duck
author: Sara Braas
note: Title page, byline, and any front/back matter removed. Chunks contain narration-only text in reading order.

chunks.text: Meep Meep Meep. Meep Meep Meep.
chunks.speaker: Pharaoh Duck (duckling)
chunks.note: duckling's own vocalization, not a narrator emotion

chunks.text: "Mama, Mama, come quick." Ava tugs at the back of her mom's gardening shirt.
Mama stands and squints. "What is it this time, nature girl?"
Meep Meep Meep
chunks.speaker: Pharaoh Duck (duckling)
chunks.note: duckling's own vocalization, same call as pd-001 but louder/faster since Ava is now closing in — not a human worry emotion

chunks.text: "A baby duck is trapped in the window hole," Ava shouts. "We have to save him."
"Don't touch that duckling, honey. It might be germy. Let me call someone," Mama says.
And just like that, she's on the phone.
"...no, it's a feral duck," Mom says on the phone in the background.
"Come here, Pharaoh Duckie, or you are going to cook in this sun."
Ava follows her fluffy Egyptian king all over the palace lawn.
"You have a Waterfowl Center?" Mom asks into her phone.
Ava gently places His Majesty in a royal basket.
Ava wonders if the royal duck knows how to swim yet. She decides to give him a lesson. Ava fills up her water table with the garden hose.
"...great, yes, we will be here..." Mom says, still on the phone.
The neighbor kids stop by. Every Pharaoh needs a court.
"His Majesty, the Duck King, has learned how to swim," Ava pronounces.
Ava lays out a picnic blanket in a shady spot and places a birdseed treat on top.
"Pharaoh Duck will take his picnic in the garden this sunny day," Ava proclaims.
The court entertains their Duck King.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: A backyard full of neighbor kids in makeshift 'royal' costumes clustered around the duckling, mid-laugh, mid-motion.

chunks.text: The court promenades with their Duck King.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: A little parade — kids marching in a line behind the duckling across the lawn.

chunks.text: The court keeps their Duck King safe.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Kids forming a protective huddle/circle around the duckling, watchful expressions.

chunks.text: The court has to go home for dinner.
chunks.note: punchline of the mock-royal conceit built up in pd-015/019-021 — comedic deflation from 'royal court' back to ordinary 'dinner'

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Kids' expressions falling/reluctant, already turning toward the house, duckling left behind on the lawn.

chunks.text: Even royals need a cuddle.
"Ava, bring the duckling, the humane society is here," Mama says.
"Aww Mama, can't we keep him?" Tears creep into Ava's eyes.
chunks.note: tearful, pleading whine — real sadness (tears) underneath the negotiating/whining delivery; keep volume soft, not a loud outburst

chunks.text: "No, baby." Mama smiles down at the fluffy, little hatchling. "He needs time to grow and a safe place to do it."
Ava wipes her tears. "But His Majesty was just about to have his bubble bath."
chunks.note: whining over a trivial detail (the bubble bath) mid-cry — classic kid whine, still tender/upset underneath

chunks.text: "His Majesty?" Mama says. "You're funny."
"Are you sure he will be okay?"
Mama gives Ava and Pharaoh Duck a quick cuddle too.
Then they wash their hands very well.
chunks.note: deadpan/ironic callback to the 'germy'/feral duck worry raised in pd-006/pd-008 — the joke is quiet and knowing, not broad comedy. Stress the word 'very' as the punch word.

chunks.text: "The High Society will transport you to your castle now, Your Majesty," Ava whispers to Pharaoh Duck.
chunks.note: whispered delivery — low volume but high emotional intensity (tender farewell)

chunks.text: And they do.
Two months later Ava is sure she sees her Pharaoh Duck flying overhead to his palace by the lake.

scenes.description: Running joke across the book: an ordinary backyard duckling is treated with mock-royal ceremony ('Pharaoh', 'His Majesty', 'the court', 'promenades'). The humor comes from the gap between elevated language and the mundane reality of a stray duckling. 'build' chunks should carry a light whimsical undertone even when their own emotion tag is something else (e.g. Playful/Silly, Joyful/Happy). 'payoff' chunks are where the joke should audibly land — a small comedic beat/deflation. 'callback' explicitly references the motif by name.

Mom's phone call to the Waterfowl Center runs in the background of the main action, intercut across several pages. These lines should stay audio-subordinate (background/muffled treatment) regardless of their own emotion tag, so they read as overheard rather than addressed to the listener.

Mama initially worries the duckling is 'germy'/feral and won't let Ava touch it without calling for help. The payoff lands quietly much later: after all the cuddling, the family simply washes their hands 'very well' — a dry, knowing callback to that early concern rather than a big joke. Emphasize 'very' and keep delivery understated/wry, not broadly comedic.

book_profile.narrator_stance: close, warm, theatrical — full expressive range, big swings encouraged
